controls.title: Know where personal information is processed
controls.statement: Define personal information for the organisation, identify the activities and systems that process it, record the holdings, and document the authority for that processing.
controls.risk: The organisation may collect or expose personal information without knowing where it is held, why it is needed or whether it is authorised.
controls.scope: Systems, applications, projects, datasets and business activities that collect, use, store, transmit or disclose personal information.
controls.examine: Reconcile privacy definitions, processing inventories, data maps and system records with collection points, business activities, legal authorities, owners and retained information.
controls.interview: Ask privacy, business and system owners how new processing is identified, its authority is established and undocumented holdings are corrected.
controls.test: Sample business processes and systems handling personal information and trace each to an inventory entry, accountable owner, documented authority and current description of processing.
controls.expected: Personal-information processing is identifiable, owned, documented and supported by a current authority before it occurs.

mappings.basis: Requires the organisation to define personal information in the context of its business activities.
Requires identification of business activities that collect, process, store or transmit personal information.
Requires personal-information holdings to be documented.
Requires a maintained inventory of systems, applications and projects that process personally identifiable information.
Requires the authority for processing personally identifiable information to be documented and processing limited to what is authorised.

controls.title: Limit personal information to authorised purposes
controls.statement: Process personal information only for documented, authorised and compatible purposes, apply the organisation's handling requirements, and minimise its use where real data is unnecessary.
controls.risk: People may suffer harm and lose trust if their information is used beyond their expectations, retained without need or exposed in avoidable copies.
controls.scope: Collection, use, disclosure, storage, testing, training, research and public posting of personal information.
controls.examine: Compare privacy notices, policies and stated purposes with collection fields, consent mechanisms, actual data flows, access, retention and use of production data outside production.
controls.interview: Ask privacy and business owners how they judge compatible use, minimise data and approve changes to existing processing.
controls.test: Sample personal-data fields and secondary uses and verify that each is necessary for a stated authorised purpose, handled as required and removed or substituted when unnecessary.
controls.expected: Personal information is processed only for a documented authorised purpose, with unnecessary collection and secondary copies prevented or removed.

mappings.basis: Requires handling requirements for personal information to be defined in the privacy policy.
Requires documented processing purposes, public descriptions, compatible processing and monitoring of processing changes.
Requires mechanisms for informed consent before collecting personal information where consent is the applicable basis.
Requires personal information used for testing, training and research to be authorised and minimised.
Requires informed consent for collecting, using and disclosing personal information in the specific context of security-clearance assessment and management.
Advises personnel about the security risks of posting personal information on online services rather than governing organisational processing generally.

controls.title: Manage privacy risks, requests and breaches
controls.statement: Assess privacy risks, provide a documented way to handle enquiries and correction requests, and include personal-information breaches in incident response.
controls.risk: A privacy concern or breach could cause greater harm and regulatory exposure if the organisation cannot identify affected people, correct records or respond promptly.
controls.scope: Privacy risk records, enquiries, complaints, correction requests and incidents involving personal information.
controls.examine: Review privacy risk entries, request and complaint procedures, case records, breach playbooks, impact assessments, notification decisions and lessons applied.
controls.interview: Ask privacy and incident leaders how requests are verified and resolved, how harm is assessed and how legal or oversight notification decisions are made.
controls.test: Trace a sample privacy request and run a personal-information breach scenario, verifying ownership, identity checks, impact assessment, correction or containment and documented notification decisions.
controls.expected: Privacy risks are visible and owned, requests are resolved through a controlled process, and breaches trigger a coordinated assessment and response.

mappings.basis: Requires privacy risks to be identified, assessed and documented in a risk register.
Requires a documented process for privacy enquiries, complaints and correction of personal information.
Requires incident-response plans to consider data breaches involving personal information.
Requires incident plans for personal-information breaches to address notification, harm assessment, mitigation and applicable privacy requirements.
